theme: Sky and Earth as a pair (West 2007 ch. 4)

plan.english: Father Sky, Mother Broad One, hear us!

notes: The vocative pair of RV 6.51.5 (dyaùḥ pítar, pŕ̥thivi mā́tar); Ζεῦ πάτερ in prayer; Latin Iu(p)piter is the univerbated vocative *dyéw ph₂ter. 'The Broad One' is *pl̥th₂wih₂, the feminine of pléth₂us used as Earth's name: Ved. pr̥thivī́ and OE Folde, which the ploughing charm addresses as mother ('Folde, fīra mōdor'). Interpolated: ḱlew- 'hear' (aorist imperative dual, cf. śr̥ṇutam in RV 1.89.4, a Dyaus–Pr̥thivī stanza, though there addressed to the Aśvins) and enclitic nos 'us' (Ved. naḥ in 6.51.5b). Ved. ádhruk 'guileless' has no cognate in the other branches and is left out. Revised: pléth₂us is no longer claimed: OE folde is a different formation (root-level), and pr̥thivī́ is Vedic only. Shared with Old English is Earth addressed as 'mother' (Ved. mā́tar = OE mōdor). Engine issues not fixable in a plan: the feminine pl̥th₂éwih₂ has the Greek-type *-ew-ih₂ where Ved. pr̥thivī́ points to *pl̥th₂wih₂, and its vocative keeps -ih₂ (Ved. pŕ̥thivi has short -i). RV 6.51.5, Il. 3.276 and Cato Agr. 134.3 checked locally; the Æcerbot charm is not in local corpora.

theme: Sky and Earth as a pair (West 2007 ch. 4)

plan.english: Sky is my father, and the Broad One is my mother.

notes: Vedic pairs Dyaus 'father' with Pr̥thivī 'mother' (RV 1.89.4; 1.164.33 dyaúr me pitā́ ... mātā́ pr̥thivī́; AV Paipp. 5.21.1 Dyáuś ca naḥ pitā́ Pr̥thivī́ ca mātā́). Latin: Varro's 'Iuppiter pater ..., Tellus mater' (West doubts its antiquity) and Lucretius' pater aether / mater terra; OE Folde (= pr̥thivī́) is 'mother'. Copula removed: the daughters have a nominal sentence at RV 1.164.33 (dyaúr me pitā́ ... mātā́ pr̥thivī́, no verb) and AV Paipp. 5.21.1; Lucr. 1.250–251 (pater aether ... matris terrai), Varro and the OE charm have the pair in apposition, also without a copula. The Vedic nominal sentence is followed: it is the older witness. Revised after round 4: the possessive is now 'my' (enclitic *moy), as in the cited parallel RV 1.164.33 (dyaúr me pitā́ … bándhur me mātā́ pr̥thivī́, VedaWeb me GEN SG in both halves); the earlier 'our' came from AV Paipp. 5.21.1 naḥ, which is not among the cited refs (r4). The possessive is Indo-Iranian only, so it is interpolated for the line as a whole. Revised: Varro (Tellus is not cognate; RR 1.1.5 checked locally in latin-ogl-latin, phi0684.phi002.ogl-lat1.xml, section 5 under 1.1) and the second Vedic stanza (RV 1.89.4) are support only; pléth₂us is no longer claimed (OE folde is root-level). Lucretius has pater aether / mater terra, so only the kin terms are cognate there. RV 1.164.33, 1.89.4 and Lucr. 1.250–251 checked locally; the Æcerbot charm is not in local corpora. Late witness (r4): Lucretius' pater aether / mater terra is a Greek philosophical topos, so it is a derivative witness; it carries only the kin terms. Engine form (r1/r2/r4 P6, open): the engine prints the feminine of pléth₂us as pl̥th₂éwih₂, the Greek εὐρεῖα type in *-ew-ih₂. Ved. pr̥thivī́ points to *pl̥th₂wih₂ (review), with the accent on *-íh₂ after u-stems in L&Y §3.2 (*pl̥th₂wíh₂, Ved. pr̥thvī́; docs/audits/engine-sweep/feminine.md records this as the dissent). No usable lexeme or plan option yields that form (pie-lex-plth2ewih2 is not usable and has the same -éwih₂); it needs an f_strong override for pie-lex-pleth2us in the lexicon, outside the plan. *pléth₂us is not claimed as secure.

Ved. mahé pitré divé 'for great Father Heaven' (RV 1.71.5) and máh- of Dyaus (3.54.2, 1.22.13); Homer has Ζεῦ πάτερ ... μέγιστε (Il. 3.276) and Διὸς μεγάλου (Il. 2.134 and often). The dative of the honoured god follows the Vedic. Interpolated: the verb h₁erkʷ- 'praise, sing' (Ved. arca, RV 3.54.2: Indo-Iranian only), 1st sg.

The formula is 'Sky's rain': Homeric Διὸς ὄμβρος (Il. 5.91 and often) = Vedic divó vr̥ṣṭí- (RV 5.83.6a diváḥ ... vr̥ṣṭím 'the rain of Dyaus'; West 2007 ch. 4). Only the genitive *diwés is cognate; the heads differ (ὄμβρος against vr̥ṣṭí-). The head n̥bʰrós follows the Greek: ὄμβρος is cognate with Ved. abhrá- 'rain-cloud' (RV 5.63.4c abhréṇa vr̥ṣṭyā́ ... diví, support) and Lat. imber (Lucr. 1.250, support), but no Vedic passage joins abhrá- with diváḥ, so the head is interpolated (Greek only) and the line is weak by the head-of-formula rule. Interpolated: the verb h₂wers- 'rain' (Ved. várṣanti; the engine has only the aorist of the root: gnomic aorist). Revised: RV 5.84.3 had been misconstrued (there diváḥ goes with vr̥ṣṭáyaḥ and abhrásya with vidyútaḥ); the locative 'upon the earth' is dropped. Il. 5.91, RV 5.83.6, 5.63.4, 5.84.3 and Lucr. 1.250 checked locally.

plan.english: The immortals made the two eyes of Sky.

notes: Ved. divó ... akṣī́ 'the two eyes of Heaven' (sun and moon, RV 1.72.10) corresponds etymologically, dual for dual, to Homeric Διὸς ὄσσε (Il. 14.286); West 2007 ch. 4 n. 25. Interpolated (Vedic only): the subject amŕ̥tāḥ 'the immortals' and the verb, the imperfect of the nasal present kʷr̥néw- (Ved. ákr̥ṇvan).

plan.english: You hold the earth and the clouds.

notes: Hittite to Wašezzili 'you hold heaven and earth' (KUB 8.41 ii 6′; again to the Storm-god ii 12′); Zarathushtra 'who holds the earth below and the heavens (nabā̊) from falling?' (Y. 44.4). PIE *nébʰos 'cloud' is the word for 'sky' in Hittite nēpis and Avestan nabah-; the English keeps the PIE gloss. Interpolated: the verb, Indo-Iranian *dʰer- 'hold' (Av. dərətā, Ved. dādhā́ra; here the causative present, Ved. dhāráyati), since Hittite uses ḫark-; 2nd sg pro-drop after the Hittite.

plan.english: The earth is a broad seat for the gods.

notes: Heaven and Earth are urvī́ sádmanī 'the two broad seats' (RV 1.185.6); Earth is ἕδος ἀσφαλές of the immortals (Hes. Th. 117f.) and εὐρυεδὴς χθών 'broad-seated earth' (Simonides); kṣā́m ... urvī́m = εὐρεῖα χθών. Ved. sádman- (*sed-mn̥) and Gk ἕδος (*sédos, = Ved. sádas-) are the same root. 'For the gods' is interpolated: Ved. devā́nām and Gk ἀθανάτων are different words. Revised: the parallel is RV 1.185.6 urvī́ sádmanī 'the two broad seats' against Simonides' εὐρυεδὴς χθών 'broad-seated earth' (a compound; not in local corpora): root-level for 'seat' (sádman- against -εδής). Hesiod's ἕδος and RV 6.17.7 (the source of 'earth' in Vedic) are other passages, support only, so dʰéǵʰōm is no longer claimed. RV 1.185.6 and 6.17.7 checked locally.

εὐρεῖα χθών = Ved. kṣā́m ... urvī́m (West 2007 ch. 4, 'Attributes of Earth'); the Greek earth 'nourishes' (τρέφει, Il. 11.741). The verb and object come from the Gathic 'this earth that bears us' (Y. 38.1 imąm ... ząm ... yā nā̊ baraitī): bʰer- and nos are Indo-Iranian only, so interpolated.

plan.english: Heaven, the ornament of the stars.

notes: The heaven that Mazdā wears is stəhr-paēsah- 'star-ornamented' (Yt. 13.2–3; Av. paēsah- = *péyḱos exactly); Agni 'adorned the vault with stars' (RV 1.68.10, Ved. piś-); Euripides' ἀστέρων ποικίλματα (Hel. 1096, cited from West 2007 ch. 9) has the same root (cf. ποικίλον ἀστερόεντα, Il. 16.134, of a breastplate). 'Heaven' is h₂éḱmō (Av. asman- 'heaven', Ved. áśman- 'stone'): Iranian only, interpolated. Copula removed: the daughters have no predication, only attributive phrases (Yt. 13.3 vaŋhanəm stəhrpaēsaŋhəm, the star-ornamented garment of heaven; Eur. Hel. 1096 ἀστέρων ποικίλματα), so the line is a noun phrase with the star-ornament in apposition to heaven. Root-level throughout (Av. compound, Ved. verb, Gk noun ποίκιλμα). Yt. 13.3 (= CAB YtFra2.3) and RV 1.68.10 checked locally; Eur. Hel. 1096 checked locally in GLAUx 0006-014 (ἀστέρων ποικίλματα). Round 4 (docs/audits/tier2-review-r4.md): stays rejected: the NP head 'heaven' (*h₂éḱmō) is interpolated and *péyḱos is exact only inside the Avestan bahuvrihi stəhrpaēsah-, which qualifies the garment, so no daughter has the apposition 'heaven, the ornament of the stars' and only the genitive 'stars' (periphery) is exact.

The Aśvins are Divó nápātā 'grandsons/offspring of Dyaus' (RV 1.182.1 divó nápātā, accusative dual in a chain of epithets, objects of mádatā; checked), the Dioskouroi Διὸς κοῦροι 'youths of Zeus' (Hymn. Hom. 33.1; checked locally in GLAUx 0013-033: Διὸς κούρους). Only the genitive of *dyḗws is shared: κοῦροι is another word, and Lith. Diẽvo sūnẽliai has *deywós. Interpolated: népōts (Vedic only; Latin 'Iouis nepotes' is West's illustration) Copula removed: the daughters have an epithet phrase, not a predication, at RV 1.182.1 (VedaWeb tags nápātā ACC DU) and Hymn. Hom. 33.1 (Διὸς κούρους, object of 'sing'), so the line is a noun phrase. Revised to this epithet line on a different Vedic stanza: the old 'grandsons of Sky, come!' on RV 10.61.4 duplicated divine-twins-001. Round 4 (docs/audits/tier2-review-r4.md): stays rejected: the head népōts is Vedic only (RV 1.182.1 diváḥ nápātā); the Greek head κοῦροι is not cognate and Lith. Dievo sūneliai has *deywós, so only the genitive *diwés is shared.

Ved. dyaúḥ pitā́ janitā́ 'Dyaus the father, the begetter' (RV 4.1.10, VedaWeb: all three NOM SG, in apposition to the subject of ákr̥ṇvan; also 1.164.33); Catullus calls Iupiter (< *dyew-ph₂ter) diuum genitor (64.26–27, LASLA: genitor NOM SG). Greek πατὴρ ἀνδρῶν τε θεῶν τε (Il. 1.544) is the same idea in other words. Copula removed: the daughters have apposition at RV 4.1.10 and Catull. 64.26–27 (Iuppiter ipse, ipse … divum genitor). RV 1.164.33 has a nominal sentence (dyaúr me pitā́ janitā́), but it is not a cited parallel here and sky-father-002 already renders it. Revised after round 4: (1) 'of the gods' is dropped. In the Vedic it came from RV 1.185.6 (devā́nām … jánitrī), a different hymn where the begetters are Heaven and Earth (VedaWeb: jánitrī ACC DU fem.), not Dyaus, so it was stitched; RV 1.185.6 is now support only. The genitive stands in the Latin alone (diuum genitor). (2) The agent noun is the suffix-accented *ǵenh₁tḗr (pie-lex-gjenh1texr), as Ved. janitā́ (oxytone) in the cited stanza; the root-accented ǵénh₁tōr is contradicted by it. Lat. genitor does not show the accent. Caveats: Iuppiter carries *dyēws and *ph₂tḗr only as compound members; Catullus 64 is a Hellenistic-modelled epyllion, and diuum genitor may belong to the divom pater type that Ennius modelled on Homer. Builder (2026-10-25 targeted evidence refresh): pie-lex-gjenh1texr now receives exact evidence in Indo-Iranian and Italic; *ph₂tḗr still receives level none (Iuppiter carries it only as a compound member). Editorial review and eval-grade decisions are retained unchanged.

plan.english: Father Sky has cast me forth to you.

notes: The divine messenger's credential: Iris 'Father Zeus sent me forth to tell you this' (Il. 11.201 Ζεύς με πατὴρ προέηκε, checked). Plaut. Amph. 19–20 (checked) is only a situational parallel: there Iouis belongs to 'Iouis iussu' (19) and 'pater ... meus' to a separate clause (20), so Latin does not attest *dyḗws ph₂tḗr as a phrase; it contributes cognate words (Iouis, pater, me) in the same situation. The verb follows the Greek: προ-έ-ηκε is pró + the k-aorist of *Hyeh₁- 'throw, cast' (a Greek/Italic formation); the English keeps the lexicon's sense. Latin misit is another root, so the verb is interpolated.

theme: Sky and Earth as a pair (West 2007 ch. 4)

plan.english: I ask Sky and the Broad One, the Mother.

notes: The ploughman's prayer to Sky and Earth. Parallel: the OE field charm prays to earth and heaven and hails 'Folde, mother of men' (Æcerbot; not in local corpora), and Vedic praises Heaven and Earth together (RV 3.54.2 divé pr̥thivyaí, checked); the Earth name *pl̥th₂wih₂ (Ved. pr̥thivī́, OE folde) is shared only at root level (folde is another formation). Support only: Hesiod's 'pray to Zeus of the Earth and pure Demeter' at the first ploughing (Op. 465; Δημήτηρ is not Earth as *pl̥th₂wih₂; not in local corpora) and Cato's 'Iupiter ... bonas preces precor' (Agr. 134.2, corrected from 134.3; a prayer to Janus and Jupiter; checked). Interpolated: the verb, the -sḱé- present of *preḱ- 'ask' (Latin precor has the root; OE biddan is another word), and 'mother' (OE mōdor only among the parallel refs). The engine's pl̥th₂éwih₂ (Greek-type *-ew-ih₂) is an engine issue.

plan.english: The daughter of Sky is born.

notes: Divó duhitā́ 'daughter of Dyaus' is uniquely Uṣas's title (over thirty times; 'at whose yoking the daughter of Dyaus is born', RV 10.39.12); Greek Διὸς θυγάτηρ is used of Helen (Od. 4.227), Aphrodite and the Muse; Lithuanian Diẽvo dukrýtė (of the Sun) has *deywós, so only dʰugh₂tḗr is shared there. Interpolated: the present middle of ǵenh₁- 'be born' (Ved. jā́yate; Gk γίγνομαι is the reduplicated present used here).

plan.english: He is the master of the house.

notes: *déms pótis 'master of the house' (West 2007 ch. 3: Ved. dáṃpatiḥ, Av. də̄ṇg paitiš, Gk δεσπότης, 'applicable in either the human or the divine sphere'). Vedic keeps it as a phrase with the old genitive dán (< *dém-s): pátir dán of Agni (RV 1.149.1) and of Indra (10.99.6 sá íd ... pátir dán), beside the compound dámpati- (Agni, 1.127.8; vocative dampate 5.22.4); Avestan has the same phrase, də̄ṇg patōiš (Y. 45.11, genitive); Greek has only univerbated forms: δεσπότης (with -της for -τις; not in Homer, cited from West) and the Homeric feminine δέσποινα 'mistress (of the house)' (Od. 14.9, checked in the treebank), *dems-pot-n-ih₂, which is the Greek ref; it shares the genitive *dems- and the root of pótis, not the formation (root-level for 'master'). The engine's genitive déms + pótis renders the phrase (it does not build consonant-stem first members, so no compound). Vedic and Avestan are one branch, so the line rests on Indo-Iranian + Greek, and in Greek only as a compound word. Interpolated: the copula (the Vedic has sá with a verb of motion, 1.149.1, or of subduing, 10.99.6); só follows Ved. sá. All Vedic and Avestan loci checked locally.
